m6_status: VALIDATED (2026-09-17) -- closed explicitly by the project owner (Bacem Ben Soui) on the basis of two independent genuinely-external executions (see m6_hash_integrity_incident_2026-09-17 and JOURNAL_DE_BORD.md)
m7_status: IMPLEMENTATION (local), fact-proposer scope only (LLM as independent witness over the existing structured corpus, not a free-text parser). Local Ollama backend, independent of the production repo's llm/ollama_backend.py -- options presented explicitly, this one chosen to avoid reopening the zero-coupling boundary and avoid managing an API key/cost.
m7_llm_fact_proposer: m7_llm_fact_proposer_v0_1.py + m7_corpus_from_llm_v0_1.py -- LLM proposals are always classified GROUNDED_ANALOGY (never GROUNDED_DIRECT or UNGROUNDED_HUMAN), fed through the same real acquire_cold_start()/evaluator machinery as M4/M6. A real bug was found and fixed before any result was kept: the first prompt version leaked the real predicted value directly into the instruction and the JSON answer example, so the model just echoed it back (spurious 16/16 SUPPORTED). Fixed by never mentioning the real value; regression-guarded by test_predicted_object_is_never_present_in_the_prompt. Real result after the fix (llama3.2:latest, corpus v0.2, 2026-09-17): 16/16 CONTRADICTED -- a genuine empirical finding (the small local model lacks a basis to answer correctly for several of these subjects, e.g. Alice never appears as a MERE_DE source in discovery_facts) not a mechanism defect. Live-LLM results are not pinned to an exact value anywhere (non-deterministic across runs/models/hardware, unlike every deterministic M6 mechanism); tests/test_m7_live_ollama_demo_v0_1.py asserts only guaranteed structural properties and skips cleanly when Ollama is unreachable, keeping the main suite portable. See MetaHIA_M7_LLM_Fact_Proposer_V0_1.md.
m7_lan_fallback_2026-09-17: Configured at explicit user request: local Ollama (LOCAL_HOST/LOCAL_MODEL) as primary, LAN sandbox server (192.168.1.11:11434, model qwen2.5-coder:7b, consistent with this project's established WP18 local-model precedent) as fallback -- triggers only on genuine unreachability, never on a merely-unusable-but-reachable response. Network endpoint choice only, no code dependency on llm/ollama_backend.py. Two real bugs found and fixed before keeping this: (1) the first live fallback attempt timed out at 30s on a cold model load on the shared LAN server (network itself was 78ms) -- fixed with a longer fallback_timeout=90s; (2) after a successful fallback, LLMProposal.model still named the requested primary model rather than the one that actually answered -- fixed by having ollama_generate_json_with_fallback() return (response, model_used) instead of a bare dict, verified end to end with local genuinely stopped. Also fixed the live demo test's reachability probe, which was using a full /api/generate call (needs a loaded model) with only 5s timeout -- switched to the lightweight /api/tags endpoint. 356/356 tests passing, zero regression. See MetaHIA_M7_LLM_Fact_Proposer_V0_1.md Sec.5.

m6_hash_integrity_incident_2026-09-17: A genuinely external reviewer running the delivered zip package (commit 613c4cd) found m6_corpus_from_m4_m5_v0_1.py's actual hash (d78ebf1b...) did not match the frozen f075f730... in the M6 v0.1 protocol. Root cause: commit 634126a had mistakenly added a convenience constant to that already-frozen file instead of putting it elsewhere. No test outcome was affected (purely additive change), but hash integrity was genuinely broken. Fixed by reverting the file to its exact frozen byte content and moving the dependent test's constant to a local definition. All 13 hashes across both M6 protocols re-verified individually after the fix. A second, independently environmented reviewer (Python 3.11.2 / pytest 7.2.1) then confirmed 338/338. On this evidence the project owner explicitly closed the validation step -- a governance decision by the project owner, not a self-declaration by the assistant. See JOURNAL_DE_BORD.md for the full chronology.

m6_non_degenerate_evidence: m6_corpus_from_m4_m5_v0_2.py + corpus/family_tree_verification_claims_v0_1.json -- an independent, deliberately partly-wrong adversarial verification-claims corpus (option chosen explicitly among 3 designs: adversarial corpus / production verifier / human annotation, to stay within the isolated-repo boundary). Separates structural prediction (replay, unchanged) from independent verification (claim agreement/disagreement), keyed by full skeleton so length-2 (derived) patterns are covered alongside length-1 (direct) ones. Real result: 26 records, genuine outcome diversity at both depths (16 SUPPORTED, 10 CONTRADICTED), holdout Brier=0.48125, ECE=0.025 (seed=0) -- first non-degenerate M6 calibration result. See MetaHIA_M6_Structural_Learning_V0_1.md Sec.6-8.
